content.user_title: Refactor Repetitive Code With DRY Steps
content.value_statement: Duplicate logic makes code harder to maintain and test. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through safe DRY refactoring steps.
actual_capabilities: Identifies obvious, structural, and logic-level duplication in source code.
Guides abstraction into functions, classes, modules, constants, or configuration.
Replaces repeated implementations with a shared unit while preserving behavior.
Includes verification checklists for unit tests, integration tests, and manual checks.
Explains common DRY mistakes, including over-abstraction and partial replacement.
limitations: It is a guidance-only skill and does not execute refactors by itself.
It cannot prove behavior is preserved without tests or manual validation.
It does not replace architecture review for large or risky refactors.
Examples use multiple languages, so users must adapt patterns to their codebase.

use_cases.title: Remove Repeated Service Logic
use_cases.description: Backend engineers can extract shared validation, pricing, or data access logic while keeping behavior stable.

use_cases.title: Standardize Frontend Helpers
use_cases.description: Frontend developers can consolidate repeated formatting, state handling, or component logic into reusable helpers.

use_cases.title: Review Refactoring Plans
use_cases.description: Engineering leads can use the checklist to evaluate whether a proposed abstraction is simple and tested.

prompt_templates.title: Find Repetition
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this code for DRY issues. List repeated logic, magic values, and similar control flow before suggesting changes.

prompt_templates.title: Extract a Simple Helper
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DRY workflow to extract one clear helper from this repeated code. Keep behavior unchanged and explain the tests to run.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-file Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a step-by-step DRY refactoring plan for these related files. Identify the shared abstraction, migration order, and verification checks.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate an Abstraction
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this proposed abstraction for over-abstraction, hidden coupling, performance impact, and incomplete replacement. Recommend specific improvements.

output_examples.input: A user service and product service repeat required-field validation.
output_examples.output: The skill would identify shared validation logic, propose a small reusable validator, and list unit and integration checks.

output_examples.input: A pricing module repeats discount rates in several calculation paths.
output: Centralize discount rates in one configuration location.
Replace each repeated calculation with a shared pricing helper.
Run existing pricing tests and add edge cases for invalid rates.

output_examples.input: A proposed utility accepts many options and callbacks.
output_examples.output: The skill would flag possible over-abstraction and recommend splitting the utility into smaller domain-specific helpers.

best_practices: Refactor one small duplicate area at a time and verify immediately.
Separate stable logic from variable inputs before choosing the abstraction.
Write or update tests before replacing repeated implementations.
anti_patterns: Creating a generic utility before there is clear repeated behavior.
Replacing only some duplicates and leaving competing implementations.
Moving code into an abstraction that hides domain meaning or weakens type safety.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps remove duplicate code safely by using a clear identify, abstract, replace, and verify workflow.

faq.question: Does it make code changes automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance that an AI coding tool or developer can apply to a codebase.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Can it help with magic numbers?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to move repeated numbers and strings into constants or configuration.

faq.question: How does it avoid over-abstraction?
faq.answer: It recommends waiting for clear repetition, keeping interfaces small, and checking whether the abstraction improves readability.

faq.question: What should I do before refactoring?
faq.answer: Capture current behavior with tests or manual checks, then refactor in small steps.
